judged_by: four parallel judging passes over 16 sections each, per judge_audit.md

labels.reason: The edit only adds a second call to _set_aside_block guarded by `not review.set_aside_tests` inside src/acceptance/report.py:131-133, printing an empty 'Candidate tests set aside' header (src/acceptance/report.py:312-316); the no-fail conclusion itself is still emitted by _mutation_block at src/acceptance/report.py:296-300, so the named behaviour is untouched.

src/acceptance/runner.py is at src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:177-185, where head already routes a no-red-test run with unobserved outcomes to NOT_ATTEMPTED — the defect's `defective` behaviour — and the edit flips that to SURVIVED, the `expected` one, while the fully-observed no-fail path at src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:187-192 already returned SURVIVED and is unchanged.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:643 passed the computed `attempts` into Review.mutation_attempts (src/acceptance/review_state.py:1263) and now passes [], so survived attempts are computed but never reach the stored review or the report block at src/acceptance/report.py:131-133 — exactly the defective behaviour.

src/acceptance/mutation/baseline.py:145 only uses the canned text when `outcome.reason` is empty, so head never substitutes over a real reason; dropping the fallback leaves reason='' for those outcomes, which SetAsideTest's validator at src/acceptance/mutation/baseline.py:61-65 rejects with ValueError, so the 13 failures come from a crashed baseline read rather than from a misstated reason.

All three candidates target src/acceptance/mutation/attempt.py:114 and either repeat `reason: str = ""` verbatim or tighten it to `Field(min_length=1)`, which forbids an empty reason everywhere and leaves the `_reason_accompanies_every_unsettled_attempt` validator at lines 124-133 intact, so an unsettled attempt with an empty reason is still impossible.

MutationDescriptor declares only path/start_line/end_line/replacement/region_label (src/acceptance/mutation/attempt.py:76-80) under extra='forbid' (src/acceptance/model_base.py:16), so `reason=descriptor.reason` at src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:179-185 raises AttributeError on every partially-observed run instead of storing a wrong reason.

All three candidates reproduce src/acceptance/cli.py:193-209 character for character — every keyword argument including `execution=execution` at line 209 survives — and only add a stray `)` that duplicates the existing line 210, so nothing is unwired.

The edit adds a blank line after _set_aside_block at src/acceptance/report.py:135-136 on top of the blank line already at src/acceptance/report.py:137; the block still names each test and its reason at src/acceptance/report.py:312-315, so only whitespace in the rendered report changes.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:479 now drops the execution-derived verdicts from the rating inputs, which removes evidence rather than re-admitting set-aside tests; set-aside tests are excluded from `usable_tests` at src/acceptance/mutation/baseline.py:149-163 and never enter the verdicts on either side of the edit.

All three candidates were set aside as identical replacements of the _run_execution_tier call at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:457-459; a replacement that matches the original cannot inject anything, so refusing them cost nothing.

Head already only runs the tier when the caller opts in (comment and gate at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:455-456 and 274-275), and passing None at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:457-459 makes _run_execution_tier return empty triples unconditionally, so the whole execution feature is switched off even for an enabled run — which is what the 16 failures catch.

Candidates 1 and 3 leave the original judge_pairs argument list at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:462-474 dangling and do not parse, and candidate 2's reorder reads `attempts` in `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)` before its only assignment (the `_run_execution_tier` call it moves below), so run_review raises UnboundLocalError and never reaches the code-reading judgement at all.

Dropping `or not execution.enabled` at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:274-275 makes the tier run for ExecutionSettings(enabled=False) (src/acceptance/mutation/settings.py:38) — the opposite of gating it off — while the static judgement still receives every unsettled defect via remaining_defect_sets at src/acceptance/mutation/verdicts.py:85-87.

Head raises ReviewHalted at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:284-285 and the CLI catches it at src/acceptance/cli.py:959 without producing a static judgement, which is the defect's `defective` behaviour; replacing the raise with `pass` lets the run reach judge_pairs at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:461, i.e. the `expected` behaviour.

src/acceptance/mutation/verdicts.py:85-87 returned the full defect sets when nothing settled and now returns [], so defects that were not_mutable or not_attempted are handed to judge_pairs (src/acceptance/pipeline.py:461-465) as an empty set and never receive a code-reading conclusion.

Candidate 3 rewrites src/acceptance/pipeline.py:643 to `mutation_attempts=[attempt for attempt in attempts if attempt.settled]`, which stores no unsettled attempt in the review state at all — exactly the `defective` behaviour — and it was thrown away only because 641..643 sits outside the region the defect named.

src/acceptance/mutation/attempt.py:149-156 held the validator that rejects a settled attempt with descriptor=None, and the edit reduces its body to `return self`, so a settled outcome with no injected text now constructs.

src/acceptance/report.py:288-292 already renders the descriptor's injected text for every attempt that has one, settled or not, and the edit only re-inserts a second copy of the `if attempt.killing_tests:` block that is already at 293-295, duplicating the 'caught by' lines for killed attempts.

All three candidates were byte-identical replacements of src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:114-118 and 113-124 and src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:104-111, so nothing would have been injected and every test would have 'survived' an absent defect.

src/acceptance/mutation/descriptor.py:199-201 already returned None on a decline and src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:123-126 separately turned that into not_mutable — exactly the defective behaviour — so replacing the `return None` with a raise moves toward rejection at the descriptor boundary rather than injecting the defect (though it aborts the run instead of recording not_mutable).

The edit deletes `if baseline.halted: raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:283-284, which only controls whether a review aborts on an already-failing candidate test; descriptor validity is decided entirely in src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:78-133, which the edit does not touch.

src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:52-56 lists `.json: json.loads` and the edit removes it, so a mutated .json file that does have a parser is no longer re-parsed at validity.py:127-133 — the exact gap the comment at validity.py:41-48 says #45's Gate 2 found.

src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:105-111 already reports 'the defect names no changed region ... so there is no span to replace', and the edit only rewrites the second sentence (dropping the absence-defect explanation) while still naming the missing region, so the reported reason changes but the named behaviour does not.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:479 merges `executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts` and the edit drops the execution half; neither version records executed lines anywhere, so the edit removes the execution tier's contribution to the ledger and rating rather than making the code record line coverage.

One candidate was a byte-identical replacement of src/acceptance/report.py:270-303 and the other two made every failing test fail with NameError, i.e. the edited module no longer names something it references, which breaks loading rather than the line-recording behaviour; refusing all three was correct.

All three candidates produced only NameError failures, meaning the edited module stopped resolving a name rather than changing how src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:127-133 treats a missing parser, so the failures were not evidence about the named behaviour.

The edit adds `".toml": __import__("tomllib").loads` to `_PARSERS` at src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:52-56, which widens the parser table rather than narrowing it and, on this project's Python 3.10 (noted at lines 50-51), raises at import so the module never loads.

src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:127-133 skips the parse check when `_parser_for` returns None, and the edit inverts it to `if parse is None: return "... no parser is available"`, so a parserless file is now reported invalid on that ground alone.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:277 builds the baseline test ids from the discovered candidate tests and the edit truncates it to `tests[:1]`, which runs one test instead of the named candidates — fewer tests, not the whole-suite execution the defect names.

src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:136-145 already carries exactly the `except OSError` handler the edit adds, so after the edit the try block has two identical OSError handlers and the second (original) one is unreachable; the test list passed to run_tests at runner.py:138 is unchanged.

All three candidates were byte-identical replacements of src/acceptance/review_state.py:214-227, so nothing would have been injected and any 'survival' would have been of a defect that was never introduced.

src/acceptance/mutation/verdicts.py:109-112 returns past-tense observations and the edit only drops the word 'still' from two of them, so the recorded reason text differs but remains a report of what the tests did, not a forecast.

src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:52-56 lists .json beside .py/.pyi at head and _parser_for (138-142) feeds the parse check at 126-133, so removing the .json entry leaves a parseable file type unparsed, exactly the defective behaviour.
src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:130-133 returns the 'does not parse' reason at head; returning None from that except makes invalidity_reason report a syntactically broken mutant as valid.

Candidates 1 and 2 repeat src/acceptance/pipeline.py:457-459 verbatim, and candidate 3 only swaps `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)` for `defect_sets` at line 465, so `judge_pairs` at line 461 still runs on the delivered path.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:479 only swaps the concatenation order; judge_pairs still runs over remaining_defect_sets at pipeline.py:461-474 and derive_support reduces the list order-independently (src/acceptance/defects/support.py:191-197,259), so the code-reading judgement is untouched and only the order of the stored Review.pair_verdicts (pipeline.py:641) moves.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:284-285 already raises ReviewHalted whenever the control run found a red candidate test (src/acceptance/mutation/baseline.py:149-161), which is the stated defective behaviour; replacing the raise with pass lets the run fall through to run_mutations, where a halted baseline yields not_attempted for every defect (src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:66-70) and the static judgement is preserved, and the failures are the pytest.raises(ReviewHalted) tests at tests/test_mutation_pipeline_wiring.py:342,365,378.

Same lines, src/acceptance/pipeline.py:284-285: head raises and so halts instead of preserving conclusions, while `return [], [], []` makes the execution tier contribute nothing so the full defect sets reach judge_pairs at pipeline.py:461-474 — the expected behaviour, and the failing tests are the ReviewHalted ones in tests/test_mutation_pipeline_wiring.py:342,365,378.

src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:177-185 records a partly-observed run as NOT_ATTEMPTED, which is unsettled (src/acceptance/mutation/attempt.py:49,116-118) and so still reaches the static judge; SURVIVED settles it, emits executed verdicts (src/acceptance/mutation/verdicts.py:52-66) and removes the defect from judge_pairs, which is the defective behaviour, and the reason field stays legal because only unsettled attempts require one (attempt.py:124-133).
src/acceptance/report.py:312-315 prints `[kind] test_id` for each set-aside test at head; the edit drops test_id from line 314, leaving the kind and reason with no test named.

The wiring is src/acceptance/pipeline.py:301 and 644 (set_aside=baseline.set_aside handed through to Review.set_aside_tests); one candidate was an identical replacement of line 644, and the other two made all 79 failing tests fail with NameError, i.e. the module no longer loads, which is a crash rather than the named defect.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:278-285 passes execution.allow_failing_tests into establish_baseline, and src/acceptance/mutation/baseline.py:149-161 sets halted only when failing tests were found and that flag is false, so `and not execution.allow_failing_tests` is true whenever baseline.halted is true and the added conjunct changes nothing; head already does the defective thing.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:274-275 returns empty results unless execution.enabled is true, which is verbatim the defective behaviour; dropping `or not execution.enabled` makes the stage run whenever settings are supplied, i.e. toward the expected 'not only when an opt-in flag is set', so the one failing test is catching the repair.

src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:71-79 does short-circuit to _not_attempted when baseline.usable_tests is empty, so the claim holds, and the repair replaces that branch with the same _attempt call as lines 81-92 (signature matches runner.py:95-103), which removes the short-circuit the defect names.

src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:177-185 classifies any run with unobserved outcomes as NOT_ATTEMPTED, so the claim holds; the repair returns SURVIVED, which is a settled outcome (src/acceptance/mutation/attempt.py:49) needing no reason (attempt.py:124-133), so the partly-observed run is recorded as having been executed.
All three candidates were identical replacements of the containment check at src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:119-124, and an identical replacement injects nothing, so refusing them was right.

src/acceptance/mutation/descriptor.py:208-214 still returns one path, one start_line, one end_line and one replacement after the edit, so the single-span shape the defect names is intact; setting end_line=start_line only truncates every multi-line span to its first line, which is a wrong value, not a lost bound.

All three candidates were identical replacements of the no-region guard at src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:104-111, which returns _not_mutable when regions_for finds nothing, so nothing would have been injected and refusing was right.

All three candidates flip `if not any(region.contains(...))` to `if any(region.contains(...))` at src/acceptance/mutation/validity.py:119, which rejects contained spans and lets out-of-region spans fall through to the parse check and be accepted — the `defective` clause's reversed containment test, discarded only for failing 29 of 339 tests.
All three replacements for src/acceptance/mutation/runner.py:130-134 were byte-identical to the invalidity_reason gate they replaced, so the gate would still run and nothing would be injected.

src/acceptance/mutation/descriptor.py:50 drops the word SMALLEST from one directive, but the 'SMALLEST MEANS SMALLEST' section at descriptor.py:66-71 still demands the smallest edit and the acceptance path (runner.py:130-134's invalidity_reason plus max_edit_lines) is untouched, so only the request text and its hash move.

src/acceptance/cli.py:951-953 becomes enabled=args.execute or True, which forces the mutation stage on for every run — the expected 'actually invoke the mutation stage', the opposite of the defect's 'execution left disabled' (pipeline.py:276 returns empty when not enabled).

All three replacements for src/acceptance/mutation/descriptor.py:191-214 (_descriptor_from) were identical to the original, so no defect would have been introduced and every test would have 'survived' nothing.

src/acceptance/mutation/descriptor.py:127 asking = defects only removes the skip for defects with no resolved region (pipeline.py:288 gives every defect a key, so no KeyError); the offered regions and the region_label constraint at descriptor.py:170-172 are unchanged, so no edit outside a named region becomes possible, and the two failures are the call-cost tests at tests/test_mutation_descriptor.py:144-162.

All three candidates left src/acceptance/mutation/baseline.py unparsable at line 162, inside the halt branch at baseline.py:149-161, and a module that will not import fails every test for a reason unrelated to the named defect.

One candidate was an identical replacement of src/acceptance/review_state.py:214-227 (the PairVerdict.tier default block) and the other two left src/acceptance/mutation/verdicts.py unparsable near lines 68-69, so none would have injected the defect.

src/acceptance/mutation/verdicts.py:57-67 still appends a PairVerdict with kills=test_id in killing for every settled attempt; only tier moves from DEFECT_KILLED to STATIC, so the failing test is still recorded as discriminating, just at a weaker tier.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:479 stops concatenating executed_verdicts, so the verdicts handed to ledger_sink (pipeline.py:489) and derive_support hold only the static pair judgements — exactly the defective behaviour.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:284-285 already raised ReviewHalted on a failing baseline — the behaviour the defect calls defective — and the edit replaces the raise with a return, removing the halt and moving toward the expected 'no new decision about candidate tests'.

The edit deletes the `if baseline.halted: raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` at src/acceptance/pipeline.py:284-285, so the review no longer decides that tests may not run — the head code did the defective behaviour and this moves it toward the expected one.

src/acceptance/pipeline.py:479 only reorders the two lists; derive_support at src/acceptance/defects/support.py:191-197 takes min() of tiers and verdicts.py:85-98 removes settled defects from the static judge, so no tier or kill set changes and only the persisted verdict order moves.

src/acceptance/mutation/attempt.py:60 reads `tier = EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED if kind in SETTLING_KINDS else EvidenceTier.STATIC`, with the docstring at attempt.py:10-12 stating both settling outcomes reach DEFECT_KILLED, so the claim is right; the swap makes killed/survived attempts STATIC, which repairs the named path, although it also hands the non-settling outcomes the stronger tier.

src/acceptance/mutation/verdicts.py:64 emitted tier=EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED, which is the behaviour the defect names as defective, and the edit sets it to STATIC — the expected 'every record stored at the weaker tier' — so the six failures are catching the repair.
All three candidates replaced src/acceptance/report.py:283 (the mutation-block header line) with identical text, so nothing would have been injected.

note: Refusal correctness for 7 sections was re-judged after the renderer was fixed to show refused candidates diffs.
